title: Opposite of a colimit cocone is a limit cone
statement: Let $J$ be a small category, $\mathcal C$ a category, $M:J\to\mathcal C$ a functor, and $(L,(\iota_j:M(j)\to L))$ a colimit cocone [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. The opposite category reverses all arrows and their composites. Write $M^{\mathrm{op}}:J^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}$ for the opposite functor. Then $(L^{\mathrm{op}},(\iota_j^{\mathrm{op}}:L^{\mathrm{op}}\to M(j)^{\mathrm{op}}))$ is a limit cone on $M^{\mathrm{op}}$. Explicitly, for every object $T$ of $\mathcal C$ and family $g_j:T^{\mathrm{op}}\to M(j)^{\mathrm{op}}$ satisfying $M(a)^{\mathrm{op}}\circ g_k=g_j$ for every $a:j\to k$, there is a unique $v:T^{\mathrm{op}}\to L^{\mathrm{op}}$ with $\iota_j^{\mathrm{op}}\circ v=g_j$ for every $j$.

source.place: Categories, Lemma 0032 (lemma-directed-category-system), proof: the sentence interpreting a limit in C as a colimit in the opposite category, immediately before the construction of the cofinal directed index.

mathlib_searches.query: The opposite of a colimit cocone is a limit cone
